---------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m9p0t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Controllers, MaxEpoch, None

VARIABLES epoch, inflight, holder, onbus, served

vars == <<epoch, inflight, holder, onbus, served>>

Msgs == Controllers \X (0..MaxEpoch)

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
    /\ inflight \subseteq Msgs
    /\ holder \in Controllers \cup {None}
    /\ onbus \subseteq Controllers
    /\ served \in 0..MaxEpoch

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ inflight = {}
    /\ holder = None
    /\ onbus = {}
    /\ served = 0

Grant(c) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ <<c, epoch>> \notin inflight
    /\ inflight' = inflight \cup {<<c, epoch>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, onbus, served>>

Enter(c) ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ \E e \in 0..MaxEpoch :
        /\ <<c, e>> \in inflight
        /\ e = epoch
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {<<c, e>>}
    /\ holder' = c
    /\ onbus' = onbus \cup {c}
    /\ served' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

Exit(c) ==
    /\ holder = c
    /\ c \in onbus
    /\ holder' = None
    /\ onbus' = onbus \ {c}
    /\ served' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inflight>>

Reconfigure ==
    /\ holder = None
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflight, holder, onbus, served>>

DropStale ==
    /\ \E m \in inflight :
        /\ m[2] < epoch
        /\ inflight' = inflight \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder, onbus, served>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Grant(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Enter(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Exit(c)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ DropStale

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

MutexContained ==
    onbus \subseteq (IF holder = None THEN {} ELSE {holder})
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    None = None
INVARIANT MutexContained
nl:
Scenario: A smart-home door-lock network coordinates several lock controllers that
share one critical actuator bus (the "critical resource") which only one controller
may drive at a time. A configuration coordinator issues an exclusive grant for the
current configuration epoch. Whenever the deployment is reconfigured (a controller
is added/removed or firmware rolls), the coordinator bumps the epoch number. Grant
messages travel over an unreliable mesh where messages can be reordered and stale
grants from previous epochs linger in flight.

The spec has exactly these actions: Grant (the coordinator emits one grant message
for the current epoch to some controller, at most one grant per epoch, only while
the bus is free); Enter (a controller consumes an in-flight grant whose epoch equals
the current epoch and, while the bus is free, seizes the actuator bus and becomes the
token holder); Exit (the current holder releases the bus); Reconfigure (only while
the bus is free, the coordinator advances the epoch, leaving old grant messages
stranded in flight); and DropStale (a stranded grant from an older epoch is discarded).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The set of controllers currently driving the actuator bus is always contained in the singleton of the current token holder, so no two controllers ever hold the critical resource at once.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od9m8p3t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ctrls, Slots, Free

VARIABLES gridLock, alloc, stage, done, slow

vars == <<gridLock, alloc, stage, done, slow>>

Stages == {"idle", "coarse", "fine"}

TypeOK ==
    /\ gridLock \in Ctrls \cup {Free}
    /\ alloc \subseteq (Ctrls \X Slots)
    /\ stage \in [Ctrls -> Stages]
    /\ done \subseteq Slots
    /\ slow \subseteq Ctrls

Init ==
    /\ gridLock = Free
    /\ alloc = {}
    /\ stage = [c \in Ctrls |-> "idle"]
    /\ done = {}
    /\ slow = {}

AcquireCoarse(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "idle"
    /\ gridLock = Free
    /\ gridLock' = c
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "coarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<alloc, done, slow>>

AcquireFine(c, s) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "coarse"
    /\ gridLock = c
    /\ s \notin done
    /\ \A p \in alloc : p[2] # s
    /\ alloc' = alloc \cup {<<c, s>>}
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "fine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gridLock, done, slow>>

Shed(c, s) ==
    /\ stage[c] = "fine"
    /\ <<c, s>> \in alloc
    /\ done' = done \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gridLock, alloc, stage, slow>>

Release(c) ==
    /\ stage[c] \in {"coarse", "fine"}
    /\ c \notin slow
    /\ gridLock = c
    /\ gridLock' = Free
    /\ alloc' = {p \in alloc : p[1] # c}
    /\ stage' = [stage EXCEPT ![c] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<done, slow>>

ToggleSlow(c) ==
    /\ slow' = IF c \in slow THEN slow \ {c} ELSE slow \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<gridLock, alloc, stage, done>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : AcquireCoarse(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, s \in Slots : AcquireFine(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, s \in Slots : Shed(c, s)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Release(c)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : ToggleSlow(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAlloc ==
    \A x \in alloc : \A y \in alloc : (x[2] = y[2]) => (x[1] = y[1])
=============================================================================
nl:
Scenario: A power-grid load shedder has several shedding controllers that must claim
power slots to shed. To avoid grid-wide races the design uses hierarchical locks:
a controller first takes the coarse grid lock, then, while holding it, takes a fine
per-slot allocation before actually shedding that slot. A participant can be slow but
never fails outright: a slow controller simply delays releasing its locks, so it may
sit holding the grid lock for a while, but it will still eventually act.

The spec has exactly these actions: AcquireCoarse (an idle controller takes the free
grid lock and enters the coarse stage); AcquireFine (a controller holding the grid
lock allocates a not-yet-allocated, not-yet-shed slot to itself and enters the fine
stage); Shed (a controller sheds a slot it has allocated, marking it done);
Release (a controller that is not currently slow drops the grid lock and all of its
allocations and returns to idle); and ToggleSlow (any controller flips between the
slow and responsive condition).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The allocation relation is functional in the slot coordinate, so any two allocations of the same slot must belong to the same controller, meaning a slot is never double-allocated.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m8p2t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, TLC

CONSTANTS Machines, InstA, InstB, GA, GB, Total, Nil

VARIABLES pool, hopper, vended, clock, ftoken

vars == <<pool, hopper, vended, clock, ftoken>>

Instances == {InstA, InstB}
Grp == (InstA :> GA) @@ (InstB :> GB)

RECURSIVE SumHop(_)
SumHop(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET m == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN hopper[m] + SumHop(S \ {m})

TypeOK ==
    /\ pool \in 0..Total
    /\ hopper \in [Machines -> 0..Total]
    /\ vended \in 0..Total
    /\ clock \in [Instances -> Machines \cup {Nil}]
    /\ ftoken \subseteq Machines

Init ==
    /\ pool = Total
    /\ hopper = [m \in Machines |-> 0]
    /\ vended = 0
    /\ clock = [i \in Instances |-> Nil]
    /\ ftoken = {}

TakeCoarse(i, m) ==
    /\ m \in Grp[i]
    /\ clock[i] = Nil
    /\ clock' = [clock EXCEPT ![i] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, hopper, vended, ftoken>>

TakeFine(i, m) ==
    /\ clock[i] = m
    /\ m \notin ftoken
    /\ ftoken' = ftoken \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, hopper, vended, clock>>

Draw(m) ==
    /\ m \in ftoken
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<vended, clock, ftoken>>

Vend(m) ==
    /\ hopper[m] > 0
    /\ hopper' = [hopper EXCEPT ![m] = hopper[m] - 1]
    /\ vended' = vended + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, clock, ftoken>>

ReleaseLocks(i, m) ==
    /\ clock[i] = m
    /\ clock' = [clock EXCEPT ![i] = Nil]
    /\ ftoken' = ftoken \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pool, hopper, vended>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, m \in Machines : TakeCoarse(i, m)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, m \in Machines : TakeFine(i, m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Draw(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Vend(m)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, m \in Machines : ReleaseLocks(i, m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

Conservation ==
    pool + SumHop(Machines) + vended = Total
=============================================================================
nl:
Scenario: A vending-machine network runs two independent operator instances (i1 and
i2) that both draw stock from one shared warehouse pool. Each instance owns its own
coarse lock; a machine must first take its instance's coarse lock and then a fine
per-machine token before it may pull an item from the shared pool into its local
hopper and later dispense it to a customer. Because the two instances share the pool,
their draws interleave, but no item is ever created or destroyed: every item is either
in the pool, sitting in some machine's hopper, or already dispensed.

The spec has exactly these actions: TakeCoarse (a machine takes its instance's free
coarse lock); TakeFine (a machine holding its instance's coarse lock takes the fine
token); Draw (a machine holding the fine token moves one item from the shared pool to
its hopper); Vend (a machine dispenses one item from its hopper to a customer); and
ReleaseLocks (a machine drops its fine token and its instance's coarse lock).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of items in the shared pool plus the items held across all machine hoppers plus the items already dispensed always equals the fixed initial total, so quantity is conserved.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od4m5p4t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cars, Voters, Quorum, MaxCap, Nil

VARIABLES onbelt, cap, proposal, tally, washed

vars == <<onbelt, cap, proposal, tally, washed>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ onbelt \subseteq Cars
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ proposal \in Cars \cup {Nil}
    /\ tally \subseteq Voters
    /\ washed \subseteq Cars

Init ==
    /\ onbelt = {}
    /\ cap = MaxCap
    /\ proposal = Nil
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ washed = {}

Propose(k) ==
    /\ proposal = Nil
    /\ k \notin washed
    /\ k \notin onbelt
    /\ proposal' = k
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onbelt, cap, washed>>

Vote(v) ==
    /\ proposal # Nil
    /\ v \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onbelt, cap, proposal, washed>>

Admit ==
    /\ proposal # Nil
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ Cardinality(onbelt) < cap
    /\ onbelt' = onbelt \cup {proposal}
    /\ proposal' = Nil
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, washed>>

Exit(k) ==
    /\ k \in onbelt
    /\ onbelt' = onbelt \ {k}
    /\ washed' = washed \cup {k}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, proposal, tally>>

SetCap(n) ==
    /\ n >= Cardinality(onbelt)
    /\ n <= MaxCap
    /\ cap' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onbelt, proposal, tally, washed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E k \in Cars : Propose(k)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Vote(v)
    \/ Admit
    \/ \E k \in Cars : Exit(k)
    \/ \E n \in 0..MaxCap : SetCap(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapOK == Cardinality(onbelt) <= cap
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {k1, k2, k3}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
    MaxCap = 2
    Nil = Nil
INVARIANT CapOK
nl:
Scenario: A car-wash conveyor line admits cars onto a moving belt of limited length.
Admitting a car is a safety-critical action, so it requires quorum approval from a
set of line sensors/voters rather than a single controller. An operator proposes a
waiting car, sensors cast votes, and only once a quorum of votes is gathered may the
car actually roll onto the belt, and only if the belt still has room. Cars eventually
finish and exit. The belt's rated capacity can change at runtime (segments are opened
or closed for maintenance), but it can never be shrunk below the number of cars
already on the belt.

The spec has exactly these actions: Propose (with no proposal outstanding, an operator
nominates a waiting, not-yet-washed car and clears the vote tally); Vote (a sensor adds
its vote to the outstanding proposal); Admit (once the proposal has a quorum of votes
and the belt has spare room, the car rolls on and the proposal is cleared); Exit (a car
on the belt finishes and leaves); and SetCap (the rated capacity is reset to any value
no smaller than the current occupancy).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of cars on the belt never exceeds the current rated capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od18m5p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxQuorum

VARIABLES enabled, burned, propOpen, tally, quorum

vars == <<enabled, burned, propOpen, tally, quorum>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ enabled \in BOOLEAN
    /\ burned \in BOOLEAN
    /\ propOpen \in BOOLEAN
    /\ tally \subseteq Nodes
    /\ quorum \in 1..MaxQuorum

Init ==
    /\ enabled = TRUE
    /\ burned = FALSE
    /\ propOpen = FALSE
    /\ tally = {}
    /\ quorum = MaxQuorum

Open ==
    /\ enabled
    /\ ~propOpen
    /\ ~burned
    /\ propOpen' = TRUE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enabled, burned, quorum>>

Vote(n) ==
    /\ enabled
    /\ propOpen
    /\ n \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enabled, burned, propOpen, quorum>>

FireMaster ==
    /\ enabled
    /\ propOpen
    /\ ~burned
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= quorum
    /\ burned' = TRUE
    /\ enabled' = FALSE
    /\ propOpen' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tally, quorum>>

Abort ==
    /\ propOpen
    /\ propOpen' = FALSE
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enabled, burned, quorum>>

SetQuorum(k) ==
    /\ k \in 1..MaxQuorum
    /\ quorum' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<enabled, burned, propOpen, tally>>

Next ==
    \/ Open
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Vote(n)
    \/ FireMaster
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E k \in 1..MaxQuorum : SetQuorum(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

OnceIrreversible ==
    burned => (~enabled /\ ~propOpen)
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {n1, n2, n3}
    MaxQuorum = 3
INVARIANT OnceIrreversible
nl:
Scenario: A smart-home door-lock network can perform one irreversible master action:
permanently burning a master override key into the hardware. Because it cannot be
undone, it needs quorum approval from the network's voting nodes. An operator opens a
proposal, nodes cast votes, and once a quorum is reached the master burn fires. Firing
the burn permanently disables the network's voting subsystem, so no further proposals
or votes are possible after it. The required quorum size can be re-tuned at runtime as
nodes join or leave.

The spec has exactly these actions: Open (while the network is enabled, no proposal is
open and the master has not been burned, an operator opens a fresh proposal); Vote (an
enabled network records a node's vote on the open proposal); FireMaster (an enabled
network with an open proposal that has reached quorum burns the master, which sets the
burned flag, disables the network, and closes the proposal); Abort (an open proposal is
closed with no effect); and SetQuorum (the required quorum size is re-tuned at any time).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the master override has been burned, the network is disabled and no proposal is open, so the irreversible burn can never happen a second time.

    Gateways = {p1, p2}
INVARIANT CommitCoherent

Scenario: A stock exchange runs an opening auction whose irreversible "opening cross"
(matching and publishing opening prices) must be committed via two-phase commit across
participant gateways. The coordinator prepares a round, gateways vote yes or no, and if
all vote yes the cross is committed. A privileged exchange admin may override the vote
and force the cross through even without unanimity. Either way the cross is irreversible:
a monotonic crossed flag gates every commit path so the opening cross can only ever be
performed once, even across reopened auction rounds.

or aborted round is reopened to idle, preserving the crossed flag and decision).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The crossed flag is set if and only if the recorded decision is commit, and since the crossed flag permanently gates all commit paths, the irreversible opening cross happens at most once.

    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<room, crashed, denied>>

Vote(v) ==
    /\ proposal # Nil
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ v \notin tally
    /\ tally' = tally \cup {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<room, proposal, crashed, denied>>

Admit ==
    /\ proposal # Nil
    /\ Cardinality(tally) >= Quorum
    /\ Cardinality(room) < Cap
    /\ room' = room \cup {proposal}
    /\ proposal' = Nil
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, denied>>

Leave(p) ==
    /\ p \in room
    /\ room' = room \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, tally, crashed, denied>>

Abort ==
    /\ proposal # Nil
    /\ denied' = denied \cup {proposal}
    /\ proposal' = Nil
    /\ tally' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<room, crashed>>

Crash(v) ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ v \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = {v}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<room, proposal, tally, denied>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Propose(p)
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Vote(v)
    \/ Admit
    \/ \E p \in Patrons : Leave(p)
    \/ Abort
    \/ \E v \in Voters : Crash(v)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

CapOK == Cardinality(room) <= Cap
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Patrons = {pa, pb, pc}
    Voters = {v1, v2, v3}
    Quorum = 2
    Cap = 2
    Nil = Nil
INVARIANT CapOK
nl:
Scenario: A library book-reservation system admits patrons into one shared study room of
bounded capacity. Admitting a patron requires quorum approval from a panel of branch
voter nodes: someone proposes a patron, branch nodes vote, and once a quorum approves and
the room still has room, the patron is admitted. One branch voter node can crash silently;
a crashed node casts no further votes, but since a quorum is still reachable from the
surviving nodes, admissions continue. Patrons eventually leave, and a proposal may be
aborted.

The spec has exactly these actions: Propose (with no proposal outstanding, propose a
patron who is not already in the room and clear the tally); Vote (a non-crashed branch
node adds its vote to the outstanding proposal); Admit (once the proposal has a quorum and
the room is below capacity, the patron enters the room); Leave (a patron in the room
leaves); Abort (an outstanding proposal is discarded and the patron is marked denied); and
Crash (at most one branch node crashes silently).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of patrons in the study room never exceeds its fixed capacity.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od17m1p6t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Routers, MaxRouters, Nil, Origin

VARIABLES token, ring, maxRing, acting, believes

vars == <<token, ring, maxRing, acting, believes>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ token \in Routers \cup {Nil}
    /\ ring \subseteq Routers
    /\ maxRing \in 1..MaxRouters
    /\ acting \in Routers \cup {Nil}
    /\ believes \in [Routers -> BOOLEAN]

Init ==
    /\ token = Origin
    /\ ring = {Origin}
    /\ maxRing = MaxRouters
    /\ acting = Nil
    /\ believes = [r \in Routers |-> r = Origin]

Join(r) ==
    /\ r \notin ring
    /\ Cardinality(ring) < maxRing
    /\ ring' = ring \cup {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, maxRing, acting, believes>>

PassToken(r, d) ==
    /\ token = r
    /\ r \in ring
    /\ d \in ring
    /\ d # r
    /\ acting = Nil
    /\ token' = d
    /\ believes' = [believes EXCEPT ![d] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ring, maxRing, acting>>

Act(r) ==
    /\ believes[r]
    /\ token = r
    /\ r \in ring
    /\ acting = Nil
    /\ acting' = r
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ring, maxRing, believes>>

StopAct(r) ==
    /\ acting = r
    /\ acting' = Nil
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ring, maxRing, believes>>

SetMaxRing(n) ==
    /\ n >= Cardinality(ring)
    /\ n <= MaxRouters
    /\ n >= 1
    /\ maxRing' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, ring, acting, believes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Join(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers, d \in Routers : PassToken(r, d)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Act(r)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : StopAct(r)
    \/ \E n \in 1..MaxRouters : SetMaxRing(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleActor ==
    acting # Nil => (acting = token /\ acting \in ring)
=============================================================================

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Routers = {ra, rb, rc}
    MaxRouters = 3
    Nil = Nil
    Origin = ra
INVARIANT NoStaleActor
nl:
Scenario: An airport baggage router uses a token ring so that only one router node may
drive the shared sorter at a time. The token holder is the only authorized actor. When the
token is passed, the new holder starts believing it holds the token, but the previous
holder's belief is not cleared immediately, so it becomes a stale participant that still
thinks it is in charge. Such a stale (or otherwise unauthorized) node must never actually
drive the sorter: driving is gated on genuinely holding the current token, not merely
believing it. The ring's membership capacity can be re-tuned at runtime, never below the
current ring size, and nodes join only while below capacity.

The spec has exactly these actions: Join (a node joins the ring while the ring is below its
capacity); PassToken (the token holder, while not driving, passes the token to another ring
member, who begins believing it holds the token while the old holder's stale belief
lingers); Act (a node that both believes it holds the token and genuinely is the current
token holder starts driving the idle sorter); StopAct (the driving node stops); and
SetMaxRing (the ring capacity is re-tuned at runtime to any value not below the current
ring size).

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever the sorter is being driven, the driving node is exactly the current token holder and a ring member, so no stale or unauthorized node ever drives the sorter.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m3p1t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Nodes, MaxTerm, MaxCap, Nil

VARIABLES term, leader, record, applied, recTerm, cap

vars == <<term, leader, record, applied, recTerm, cap>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ leader \in Nodes \cup {Nil}
    /\ record \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ applied \in 0..MaxCap
    /\ recTerm \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ cap \in 0..MaxCap

Init ==
    /\ term = 0
    /\ leader = Nil
    /\ record = 0
    /\ applied = 0
    /\ recTerm = 0
    /\ cap = MaxCap

Bump == IF term < MaxTerm THEN term + 1 ELSE term

Elect(n) ==
    /\ leader # n
    /\ term' = Bump
    /\ leader' = n
    /\ UNCHANGED <<record, applied, recTerm, cap>>

Update(n) ==
    /\ leader = n
    /\ record < cap
    /\ record' = record + 1
    /\ applied' = applied + 1
    /\ recTerm' = term
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, cap>>

StepDown ==
    /\ leader # Nil
    /\ leader' = Nil
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, record, applied, recTerm, cap>>

SetCap(k) ==
    /\ k >= record
    /\ k <= MaxCap
    /\ cap' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, leader, record, applied, recTerm>>

Next ==
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Elect(n)
    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Update(n)
    \/ StepDown
    \/ \E k \in 0..MaxCap : SetCap(k)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoLostUpdate ==
    /\ record = applied
    /\ recTerm <= term
=============================================================================
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Nodes = {g1, g2}
    MaxTerm = 2
    MaxCap = 2
    Nil = Nil
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
Scenario: A vending-machine network keeps one shared inventory record that only the
current leader may update. Leaders are chosen by election with failover: an election
installs a new leader and raises the term (up to a bound), and a leader may step down.
Every update the leader applies advances the record and the applied-update count together
and stamps the record with the leader's current term, so committed updates are counted
exactly once and are never lost. The number of updates that may be committed is bounded by
a capacity that can be re-tuned at runtime, never below the current record value.

The spec has exactly these actions: Elect (a node distinct from the current leader becomes
leader, raising the term up to its bound); Update (the current leader, while the record is
below capacity, advances the record and the applied count and stamps the record with the
current term); StepDown (the current leader relinquishes leadership); and SetCap (the
capacity is re-tuned at runtime to any value not below the current record value).

SAFETY PROPERTY: The record value always equals the applied-update count and its stamped term never exceeds the current term, so no committed update is ever lost or double-counted.
